items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Jack Robbins, the music publisher, long before you were born, instigated me writing this tune, and then he took the tune and gave it to Irving Caesar, who wrote the lyric to “Tea for Two,” and he also wrote the lyric for this tune.

ctx.x: He probably would. You’ll have to remind him when he comes to the concert. [laughs]

Yeah, I must remind him. But then somebody said they liked the tune, so then I was able to accept it as my own work after that. In fact, I was a little disappointed. Jack Robbins, the music publisher, long before you were born, instigated me writing this tune, and then he took the tune and gave it to Irving Caesar, who wrote the lyric to “Tea for Two,” and he also wrote the lyric for this tune. It’s not bad. It . . .
It’s not your favorite lyric, though.
